question:
(a) Prove that $\tan^{-1}x+\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ when $x>0$ and equals $-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ when $x<0$.

(b) Use the established result to evaluate $\tan^{-1}(-2)+\tan^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.
explanation:
(a)
Let
$$A=\tan^{-1}x,\qquad B=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)$$
Then
$$\tan A=x,\qquad\tan B=\frac{1}{x}$$
Using the tangent addition formula,
$$\tan(A+B)=\frac{x+\frac{1}{x}}{1-x\cdot\frac{1}{x}}$$
The denominator is $0$, so $A+B$ is an odd multiple of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Since both $A$ and $B$ lie in $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, their sum lies in $(-\pi,\pi)$.
When $x>0$, both $A$ and $B$ are positive, so $A+B>0$. Hence,
$$A+B=\frac{\pi}{2}$$
When $x<0$, both angles are negative, so $A+B<0$. Hence,
$$A+B=-\frac{\pi}{2}$$
Therefore,
$$\tan^{-1}x+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{\pi}{2}, & x>0\\-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, & x<0\end{cases}$$

(b)
Taking $x=-2$, we have $x<0$ and $\dfrac{1}{x}=-\dfrac{1}{2}$. Therefore,
$$\tan^{-1}(-2)+\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)=-\frac{\pi}{2}$$
Hence, the required value is $-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
